title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: which days are billed as detention days
content:
## Scope

This rule of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category decides how many days of a per-container record are billed on its final detention line, and which calendar days the line covers.

## Rule

1. **Separate clock model.** The detention days are the days used by the detention clock beyond its free days.
2. **Combined clock model.** The n-th day of the merged clock falls on the start date plus n calendar days. On import, the days after the full gate-out date are detention days; on export, the days up to and including the full gate-in date are detention days. The detention days billed are the chargeable days of the merged clock (the days beyond the merged free days) that are detention days.
3. A record with no detention day beyond free time gets no detention line.
4. The first and last detention day billed are the first and last chargeable detention days themselves, so a detention line that ends at a terminal movement, such as the full gate-in date of an export record, ends on that movement's date and not on the clock-stop date.

## The same rule counted in positions

On a combined record, find the position of the terminal movement in the merged clock: the calendar days from the clock start to the full gate-out date (import) or the full gate-in date (export), less the product's clock start offset, increased by one.

- **Import**: the detention days billed are the days used beyond the larger of the free days and that gate-out position, and none when the days used do not go beyond it.
- **Export**: the detention days billed are the smaller of the days used and that gate-in position, less the free days, and none when that figure does not exceed the free days.

## Worked cases (hypothetical dates and an illustrative 15 merged free days, offset of one day)

| Record | Dates | Days used | Movement position | Detention days billed | First and last billed day |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Export | empty pickup 1 July, full gate-in 20 July, loading 26 July | 25 | 19 | 4 (positions 16 to 19) | 17 July to 20 July |
| Import | discharge 1 July, full gate-out 10 July, empty return 30 July | 29 | 9 | 14 (positions 16 to 29) | 17 July to 30 July |
| Import | discharge 1 July, full gate-out 20 July, empty return 30 July | 29 | 19 | 10 (positions 20 to 29) | 21 July to 30 July |
| Export | empty pickup 1 July, full gate-in 12 July, loading 26 July | 25 | 11 | none, no detention line | none |

In the first case the line ends on 20 July, the full gate-in date, although the record's clock stopped on 26 July.
